description:
## Finding

Every workspace crate enables `#![cfg_attr(docsrs, feature(doc_cfg))]` at the top of `lib.rs`, but **no item in the workspace uses `#[cfg_attr(docsrs, doc(cfg(feature = ...)))]`**. The feature gate is enabled for nothing.

```
$ rg "doc(cfg" pkix-*/src/
(no matches)

$ rg "cfg_attr(docsrs" pkix-*/src/lib.rs
pkix-ac/src/lib.rs:2:#![cfg_attr(docsrs, feature(doc_cfg))]
pkix-chain-simple/src/lib.rs:2:... (every crate)
```

## Impact

Feature-gated public items in `pkix-path` (`EcdsaP256Verifier` behind `p256`, `RsaPkcs1v15Sha256Verifier` behind `rsa`, the entire `std::error::Error` impl behind `std`) are not visually labeled on docs.rs. Users browsing the rendered docs do not see "Available on crate feature `p256` only." badges.

Same issue in pkix-revocation: `CrlChecker` (behind `crl`), `OcspChecker` (behind `ocsp`).

## Fix

Either:

1. Add the doc-cfg attribute to each feature-gated public item:

```rust
#[cfg(feature = "p256")]
#[cfg_attr(docsrs, doc(cfg(feature = "p256")))]
pub struct EcdsaP256Verifier;
```

2. Or — easier on MSRV 1.73 — switch to `#![cfg_attr(docsrs, feature(doc_auto_cfg))]` (also nightly-only) which infers the badges automatically. This is what most RustCrypto crates do now.

3. Or remove the unused `feature(doc_cfg)` line from every crate.

## Priority

P3 — docs.rs UX. The unused `feature(...)` is also a minor code smell (says one thing, does another).
title: P3: feature(doc_cfg) enabled in every crate but no #[doc(cfg(...))] attribute exists; feature-gated items unlabelled on docs.rs
